java.say: `new LockFactory()` makes a factory object. The program reads the setting lock.supplier from a configuration file; say it is "smartlock". It passes that word to createLock().
A switch compares the word with each case, from top to bottom, and runs the one that matches.
It matches "smartlock". The factory makes a SmartLockApi, the supplier's code, and puts it inside a new SmartLockAdapter. No other class in the program names these classes.
The factory hands the new object back. The program keeps it in `lock`, whose type is BikeLock, the interface. It does not know which class is behind it, and it does not need to.
The program opens bike 42 through BikeLock. If the configuration file says "lockit" tomorrow, the factory makes another adapter, and this line does not change.

cpp.say: `LockFactory()` makes a factory object. The program reads the setting lock.supplier from a configuration file; say it is "smartlock". It passes that word to createLock().
The factory compares the word with each supplier, from top to bottom. It is not "lockit", so the factory skips that block.
The next test matches "smartlock". The factory makes a SmartLockApi, the supplier's code, and puts it inside a new SmartLockAdapter. No other class in the program names these classes.
The factory hands the new object back. The program keeps it in `lock`, whose type is BikeLock*, a pointer to the interface. It does not know which class is behind it, and it does not need to.
The program opens bike 42 through BikeLock. If the configuration file says "lockit" tomorrow, the factory makes another adapter, and this line does not change.
